what_this_is: The level half of the token-link repair. The JLPT reconcile resolved each community-list entry to a record by its READING, the same way the dissector resolved tokens, so the kana entries する 'to do', なる 'to become', くれる 'to give', かかる 'to take (time, money)' and ほう were filed on 刷る 'to print', 生る 'to bear fruit', 暮れる, 罹る and 報 'report', and the words they name were left with a stray higher-level tally. Each row moves the level, the agreement pair and level_sources onto the record the lists' own glosses name. Applied by scripts/apply_level_evidence.py --db-only --data research/derived/repairs/level_transfer_repairs.json (rebuild step after the last orthographic relink, before scripts/apply_token_link_repairs.py re-levels the touched sentences); the exporter publishes corpus/vocab/*.json.
formula: scripts/ingest/reconcile_levels.py :: assign(): level = the EARLIEST level any consulted list assigns; level_agreement = n_for/consulted over the four vocab lists (elzup, openanki, bluskyo, jlptvocabapi); level_confidence = round(n_for/consulted, 3). Spec section 1.5: at least three independent lists.
siblings_not_changed: 刷る, 生る, 罹る and 報 keep the n5 tally the lists gave the kana entry. Their own glossed entries sit at N2/N3 (openanki_vocab_n2 'する to print', jlptvocabapi_n2 刷る, jlptvocabapi_n2 生る, jlptvocabapi_n3 罹る), but lowering them now would re-level every sentence whose する/なる/かかる run still carries a sibling edge through rule R2 of scripts/ingest/build_sentence_vocab.py. After Q2 no lesson unlocks them; correcting their tallies is an open item (research/reports/q2_token_links_report.md).
